sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: Pinus edulis, the two-needle pinyon, is a slow-growing tree of dry woodlands in the southwestern United States and northern Mexico. It commonly reaches 8–17 m and develops a rounded, spreading crown.

sections.title: Needles and cones
sections.text: Its short needles, 1.5–5 cm long, grow in pairs. Cones are about 3.5–5 cm long and usually contain 10–20 soft-shelled, wingless seeds.

sections.title: Food
sections.text: The seeds are edible pine nuts and have long been gathered as food. They are distinct from the larger seeds of stone pine, P. pinea.
